It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing the “noise and clamor” of a world where the Lord’s ministers are “dragged off” by the “powers that be,” and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the enforced disappearance of pastors and the silence of unmarked graves in this hour? [207, 840, 1152, 1440, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the “savage wolves” who “do not spare the flock,” or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that “not one human sinner or demonic power will ever succeed in his rebellion” against the King? [13, 20, 368, 1143, 1425, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many seek “diplomatic relations” with a “distinctively anti-Christian agenda” to avoid the “scars” of the cross, we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Master personally governs the “record of history” through His “one continuous plan of redemption” [11, 12, 28, 722, 1288, 1316, 1391, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the disappearance of a pastor is not an “administrative anomaly” but is subject to the “decree from God” who “harnesses the deeds of the wicked to accomplish His good and perfect ends” [15, 68, 1143, 1505, 1508, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

### **Section 1: Sovereignty over the "Horrible Pit" of Imprisonment**

**Verse**
“ ‘But as for you, you meant evil against me; but God meant it for good, in order to bring it about as it is this day, to save many people alive’ ” (Genesis 50:20). [1312, 1361, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed faith—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that even when a state “makes havoc of the church” by “dragging off men and women [and] committing them to prison,” the Lord “remains with them” and uses the “horrible pit” of their suffering to “testify to the gospel of the grace of God” (Acts 8:3; 20:24) [323, 840, 975, 1152, 1440, Conversation History]. Like Joseph, who was “unjustly accused... and imprisoned,” a vanished pastor is never outside the “sovereign plan” of the King who “raises up kings, then pulls them from their thrones when they have served His administration” [15, 657, 1351, 1528, 1636, 1720, Conversation History]. Scripture reveals that while the “body of the believer” may be “incarcerated,” the “word of God is not chained,” and its “decisions are immutable” (2 Timothy 2:9) [11, 25, 41, 123, 1268, 1283, 1420, 1504, 1646, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “trade in your worry for trust,” for “nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan,” even when the “nations rage and the people plot a vain thing” (Psalm 2:1) [11, 21, 94, 121, 201, 772, 1132, 1143, 1408, 1515, 1572, Conversation History]. Recognize that “the servant is not greater than his master,” and your “sole objective” is to “adorn the doctrine of God” whether in a pulpit or a cell, knowing that “He who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ” (Philippians 1:6; John 15:20) [5, 53, 101, 176, 300, 829, 1316, 1406, 1408, 1450, 1515, 1670, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Theocracy vs. Pilgrimage**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, “national prosperity” and “dwelling in your land safely” were “temporal signs” of God’s favor [409, 991, 1313, 1353, 1519, 1546, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our vision, revealing that we are “sojourners and pilgrims” whose “victory” is found not in “carnal weaponry” but “by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony,” for “Jesus answered, ‘My kingdom is not of this world’ ” (John 18:36; Revelation 12:11) [13, 14, 21, 32, 440, 1020, 1313, 1402, 1491, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Mandate to Obey the Higher King**

**Verse**
“But Peter and the other apostles answered and said: ‘We ought to obey God rather than men’ ” (Acts 5:29). [1130, 1176, 1247, 1256, 1300, 1370, 1431, 1529, 1720, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition teaches that “secular courts” and governments are “God’s ministers” for civil peace, but they become “usurpers” when they try to “tamper with or attempt to tone down the gospel” (Romans 13:4) [19, 1121, 1144, 1316, 1473, 1529, 1638, 1720, Conversation History]. When a state “fears the multitude” and silences a pastor to satisfy “unrighteous deception,” the “church militant” is commanded to “contend earnestly for the faith” even when it is “costly and painful” (Jude 3) [92, 113, 123, 201, 1192, 1236, 1313, 1408, 1454, 1489, 1511, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. The “bondage of man” cannot cancel the “binding and authoritative mandate” of the Savior, for “if anyone does not love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed” (1 Corinthians 16:22) [123, 727, 1145, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You must “discipline your body and bring it into subjection,” refusing to let the “noise and tumult” of “political maneuvering and lobbying” replace the “spiritual service of worship” (Romans 12:1) [12, 13, 16, 17, 19, 20, 31, 79, 101, 116, 212, 1138, 1262, 1313, 1406, 1503, 1515, 1605, 1670, 1709, Conversation History]. “Never become so involved in this world” that you seek “deliverance” from a “legislative body” rather than from the “Rock of Ages,” for “perfect justice will come” from the “Lord, the righteous Judge” (Psalm 62:2; 2 Timothy 4:8) [24, 51, 109, 130, 856, 1020, 1315, 1408, 1503, 1515, 1623, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Civil vs. Spiritual Jurisdiction**
Under the **Mosaic Law**, the theocracy unified civil and religious law, but God still “removed [kings] from their thrones” when they “rejected the word of the LORD” (1 Samuel 15:23) [7, 15, 17, 1078, 1183, 1533, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “citizenship,” showing that the “church militant” is an “assembly of the citizens of heaven” whose “true home” is in a “heavenly Jerusalem,” not in any “geopolitical territory” (Philippians 3:20) [13, 26, 38, 142, 437, 440, 1255, 1313, 1320, 1321, 1342, 1426, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: Martyrdom and the Heavenly Registry (No Grave)**

**Verse**
“but you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to an innumerable company of angels, to the general assembly and church of the firstborn who are registered in heaven, to God the Judge of all, to the spirits of just men made perfect” (Hebrews 12:22–23). [1163, 1168, 1218, 1255, 1317, 1318, 1319, 1321, 1323, 1342, 1426, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Scriptures reveal that the only “registration” that truly matters is having your name “written in the Book of Life,” for the “true church” is an “intangible and invisible” spiritual house (Revelation 13:8) [17, 184, 1219, 1220, 1255, 1313, 1426, Conversation History]. Though a pastor may vanish without a “monument to their pride,” God “knows those who are His,” and they are “protected by the power of God” even when they are “reduced to skin and bones” (2 Timothy 2:19; 1 Peter 1:5) [11, 65, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 300, 361, 413, 442, 473, 1138, 1143, 1450, 1515, Conversation History]. The “record of history” shows that many “wandered in deserts and mountains, in dens and caves of the earth,” and though they had no “royal dwelling,” they are “called, chosen, and faithful” (Hebrews 11:38; Revelation 17:14) [789, 991, 1128, 1233, 1266, 1268, 1315, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that your “identity has been transformed” and “death is but a harmless shadow for the sheep of the Good Shepherd” (1 Thessalonians 1:10) [13, 24, 68, 92, 102, 142, 190, 198, 243, 248, 732, 844, 1032, 1313, 1315, 1406, 1408, 1426, 1450, 1515, 1646, Conversation History]. You can find “tranquility of soul” by fixating on the “incorruptible inheritance,” for “scars... don’t define us; our hope does” (1 Peter 1:4) [13, 14, 26, 80, 83, 102, 121, 142, 192, 193, 201, 352, 442, 730, 830, 1257, 1313, 1408, 1426, 1515, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Shadows vs. Substance**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “animal sacrifices” were “shadows” that could not “eliminate sin,” and “storage cities” were built as “monuments” to human power [11, 32, 394, 789, 1233, 1283, 1313, 1331, 1344, 1430, 1442, 1460, 1467, 1684, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this by revealing that “Christ, our Passover, was sacrificed for us,” and we now carry our “treasure in jars of clay,” making the “burial of a donkey” or the lack of a grave irrelevant to our standing as “joint heirs with Christ” (1 Corinthians 5:7; 2 Corinthians 4:7; Romans 8:17) [13, 14, 24, 121, 130, 132, 142, 623, 722, 734, 759, 906, 1016, 1018, 1032, 1100, 1132, 1192, 1313, 1323, 1403, 1406, 1426, 1431, 1445, 1471, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Final Reckoning for the Oppressor**

**Verse**
“And they cried with a loud voice, saying, ‘How long, O Lord, holy and true, until You judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?’ ” (Revelation 6:10). [16, 188, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Voddie Baucham**—teaches that “perfect justice will come” and God “harnesses the deeds of the wicked” to accomplish His “good purposes” [14, 253, 724, 1143, 1315, 1473, 1477, 1505, 1515, Conversation History]. Rulers who “think themselves much better than they really are” and “execute judgment” against the innocent will themselves be “weighed on the scales and found deficient” (Daniel 5:27) [37, 324, 1061, 1402, 1720, Conversation History]. On the Day of the Lord, every human “monument” will “vanish—like smoke they vanish away,” and “Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own” (Psalm 102:3; Revelation 11:15) [11, 13, 20, 24, 32, 35, 103, 136, 1199, 1315, 1460, 1515, 1684, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “God will wipe away every tear from their eyes” and the “blood of the Lamb” has already secured the “final triumph” over every “usurper” (Revelation 21:4) [13, 14, 21, 24, 32, 92, 94, 109, 121, 201, 352, 412, 470, 725, 816, 822, 948, 1132, 1143, 1313, 1315, 1408, 1426, 1450, 1491, 1515, 1646, 1670, 1720, Conversation History]. You can find “repose of the soul” in the truth that “His counsel shall stand, and He will do all His pleasure,” even when his shepherds are taken from us (Isaiah 46:10) [11, 21, 24, 64, 101, 116, 121, 142, 1132, 1143, 1306, 1406, 1408, 1419, 1429, 1445, 1503, 1515, 1565, 1572, 1616, 1684, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 147, 176, 211, 212, 222, 285, 300, 324, 332, 361, 405, 413, 414, 444, 449, 591, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

Not every sinner is a mass murderer or rapist. In fact, some sinners seem to be relatively good people, compared to others. But the Bible is clear about the extent of every sinner’s fallenness.
